Madrid bus electrification: line, depot and city model¶

IE Sustainability Datathon (Kearney) · Deliverable 1 · Main notebook

This notebook produces the four mandatory outputs File_1.csv–File_4.csv, the BI visualisation and every check the jury needs. It is built in dependency order: baseline → lines (File 2) → depots (File 3) → prioritisation → scenarios (File 4) → benchmark (File 1) → visualisation → compliance.

How to read it. Each section follows the same pattern: a text cell (what, why, sources, V/D/P/A label), a short code cell, then a visible output — a table, a chart or a CHECK … PASS line. The jury reads saved outputs only; a step that prints nothing counts as not done.

Helpers. fetch() downloads each source once and logs URL, date, size and checksum; assume() labels every value V, D, P or A for the assumptions register; check() prints a visible PASS / FAIL line.

In [2]:
# ---- Data register: every downloaded or manually obtained source is logged here.
DATA_REGISTER = []

def fetch(url, filename, note="", manual=False):
    """Download a public file into data_raw/ and log source, date, size and checksum.
    manual=True: the file was obtained by hand (registration/API); it must already be in data_raw/."""
    path = os.path.join(RAW, filename)
    if not manual and not os.path.exists(path):
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=120)
        r.raise_for_status()
        with open(path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(r.content)
    size = os.path.getsize(path) if os.path.exists(path) else None
    sha = hashlib.sha256(open(path, "rb").read()).hexdigest()[:12] if size else None
    DATA_REGISTER.append(dict(file=filename, url=url, downloaded=RUN_DATE, bytes=size,
                              sha256_12=sha, obtained="manual" if manual else "script", note=note))
    return path

def show_register():
    display(pd.DataFrame(DATA_REGISTER))

# ---- Provenance labels (brief section 4.6): V verified, D derived, P proxy, A assumption.
ASSUMPTIONS = []

def assume(variable, value, label, evidence, impact="", sensitivity=""):
    assert label in {"V", "D", "P", "A"}, "label must be V, D, P or A"
    ASSUMPTIONS.append(dict(variable=variable, value=value, label=label, evidence=evidence,
                            impact=impact, sensitivity=sensitivity))
    return value

# ---- Visible checks: every step prints CHECK ... PASS / FAIL.
CHECKS = []

def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    CHECKS.append(dict(check=name, result="PASS" if ok else "FAIL", detail=detail))
    print(f"CHECK {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} | {name}" + (f" | {detail}" if detail else ""))
    return ok
print("Helpers ready: fetch() logs sources, assume() labels values V/D/P/A, check() prints PASS/FAIL")

GTFS helpers. Read a feed, find the services active on a date (calendar, then calendar_dates exceptions), and measure trip length from shape_dist_traveled or the shape geometry.

In [4]:
# ---- Generic GTFS helpers (shared logic with the benchmark notebook).
def read_gtfs(zip_path, tables=("agency","routes","trips","stop_times","calendar","calendar_dates","shapes","feed_info")):
    feed = {}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = set(z.namelist())
        for t in tables:
            if f"{t}.txt" in names:
                feed[t] = pd.read_csv(z.open(f"{t}.txt"), dtype=str, low_memory=False)
    return feed

def active_service_ids(feed, date_str):
    """Service ids running on date_str (YYYY-MM-DD), applying calendar then calendar_dates exceptions."""
    d = pd.Timestamp(date_str); ymd = d.strftime("%Y%m%d"); dow = d.day_name().lower()
    active = set()
    if "calendar" in feed:
        c = feed["calendar"]
        m = (c["start_date"] <= ymd) & (c["end_date"] >= ymd) & (c[dow] == "1")
        active |= set(c.loc[m, "service_id"])
    if "calendar_dates" in feed:
        cd = feed["calendar_dates"]; cd = cd[cd["date"] == ymd]
        active |= set(cd.loc[cd["exception_type"] == "1", "service_id"])
        active -= set(cd.loc[cd["exception_type"] == "2", "service_id"])
    return active

def haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
    r = 6371.0088
    p1, p2 = np.radians(lat1), np.radians(lat2)
    dphi, dl = p2 - p1, np.radians(lon2 - lon1)
    a = np.sin(dphi/2)**2 + np.cos(p1)*np.cos(p2)*np.sin(dl/2)**2
    return 2*r*np.arcsin(np.sqrt(a))

def shape_lengths_km(feed):
    s = feed["shapes"].copy()
    for c in ("shape_pt_lat","shape_pt_lon"): s[c] = s[c].astype(float)
    s["shape_pt_sequence"] = s["shape_pt_sequence"].astype(int)
    s = s.sort_values(["shape_id","shape_pt_sequence"])
    g = s.groupby("shape_id")
    s["seg"] = haversine_km(g["shape_pt_lat"].shift(), g["shape_pt_lon"].shift(), s["shape_pt_lat"], s["shape_pt_lon"])
    return s.groupby("shape_id")["seg"].sum()

def trip_km(feed, trip_ids, dist_unit_m=None):
    """Km per trip. Preferred: shape_dist_traveled (unit must be confirmed: metres or km);
    fallback: geodesic length of the trip's shape. Prints which method each trip used."""
    st = feed["stop_times"][feed["stop_times"]["trip_id"].isin(trip_ids)]
    km = pd.Series(dtype=float)
    if "shape_dist_traveled" in st and st["shape_dist_traveled"].notna().any():
        d = st.assign(x=pd.to_numeric(st["shape_dist_traveled"], errors="coerce")).groupby("trip_id")["x"].agg(lambda v: v.max() - v.min())
        assert dist_unit_m is not None, "Confirm shape_dist_traveled unit (metres or km) and pass dist_unit_m=True/False"
        km = d / 1000 if dist_unit_m else d
    missing = set(trip_ids) - set(km.dropna().index)
    if missing and "shapes" in feed:
        lens = shape_lengths_km(feed)
        t = feed["trips"].set_index("trip_id").loc[list(missing), "shape_id"]
        km = pd.concat([km.dropna(), t.map(lens)])
    print(f"trip_km: {len(km)} trips, {len(missing)} via shape geometry fallback")
    return km
print("GTFS helpers ready: read_gtfs, active_service_ids and trip-length functions")

GTFS helpers ready: read_gtfs, active_service_ids and trip-length functions

1 · Data acquisition¶

Download every source from its public landing page and log download date, size and checksum. Files that need registration or an API key are obtained manually, placed in data_raw/ and logged with manual=True (brief 5.1). No API keys in this notebook.

Direct file URLs come from the portal's CKAN API (https://datos.madrid.es/api/3/action/package_show?id=<dataset>); the files themselves are served by datos.emtmadrid.es.

The GTFS URL is a rolling feed. EMT regenerates gtfs_emt.zip daily and its calendar starts on the generation day, so a later download is a different file. fetch() never overwrites a file already in data_raw/: keep the snapshot used for the submission and quote its SHA-256 from the register. The feed also has a frequencies.txt row for almost every trip, but those rows only describe each hour's headway: the trips in trips.txt / stop_times.txt are already individual timed runs, chained into vehicle blocks (block_id). §4 must not expand them; doing so multiplies daily km about 26× (8.8 M km instead of 0.34 M). This is the brief's "avoid double counting repeated trips" rule.

In [5]:

2 · Reference day¶

Rule (brief section 2): a Tuesday or Wednesday, regular working day in EMT's calendar, outside holidays and the summer timetable, no strikes or events, inside GTFS validity.

How we apply it. A day is eligible when it is a Tuesday or Wednesday coded LA (working day) in the standard season IV, and every weekday of its week is also LA and IV, so the week has no holiday, strike (HU), event (EV) or seasonal timetable around it.

  • Reference day (REF_DATE, used for GTFS km in File 1 and File 2) = the first eligible day inside the GTFS snapshot's validity.
  • Supply day (SUPPLY_DATE, used for peak_buses) = the latest eligible day on the same weekday in the supply data whose total peak buses (sum of each line's peak) is within a tolerance of the median eligible day. The supply data ends 31 Aug 2026 and the GTFS starts on its download day, so no single day has both; the brief allows the closest equivalent weekday in that case.

Why the typicality test. The calendar alone points to Tue 16 Jun 2026, but service and ridership that day are already 4–5 % below a normal Tuesday (the end of the school and university term). A November reference day is a full-service day, so we take the latest Tuesday that still looks like one and report 16 Jun as a sensitivity. Both dates go in the report.

Decision record · reference and supply days | Option | Verdict | Why | |---|---|---| | Calendar rule only (16 Jun 2026) | Rejected, kept as sensitivity | Service already 4.4 % below a normal Tuesday (end of term); −77 peak buses over 89 lines | | Calendar rule + typicality within 3 % (9 Jun 2026) | Chosen | Latest real day that looks like a full-service day, as a November reference day is | | Median of all eligible Tuesdays, line by line | Rejected | Smoother, but not a published day; the brief asks for a day's supply data | | A Wednesday instead of a Tuesday | Rejected | The supply day must match the reference day's weekday, and 17 Nov is the first eligible day in GTFS validity |

Disruption check: whether known works (A-5/M-30, Metro L10) distort the reference day is tested at the end of §4, where line km and peak buses exist.

In [7]:
# Eligible days: Tue/Wed, working day, standard season, in a fully regular Mon-Fri week.
cal = emt_cal.assign(date=pd.to_datetime(emt_cal.Fecha)).sort_values("date")
cal["dow"] = cal.date.dt.dayofweek                               # 0 = Monday
cal["week"] = cal.date.dt.to_period("W-SUN")
cal["regular"] = (cal.TipoDiaEs == "LA") & (cal.TemporadaTG == "IV")
week_ok = cal[cal.dow < 5].groupby("week").regular.all()
cal["regular_week"] = cal.week.map(week_ok).fillna(False).astype(bool)
eligible = cal[cal.dow.isin([1, 2]) & cal.regular & cal.regular_week]

gtfs_start = pd.to_datetime(gtfs_cal["calendar"].start_date.min())
gtfs_end = pd.to_datetime(gtfs_cal["calendar"].end_date.max())
ref = eligible[eligible.date.between(gtfs_start, gtfs_end)].iloc[0]
REF_DATE = assume("Reference day", ref.Fecha, "D",
                  "First Tue/Wed in GTFS validity coded LA + IV with a fully regular Mon-Fri week (EMT calendar)")

# Supply-day candidates: same weekday, same rule, inside the supply data. Typicality = sum of each line's peak buses.
TYPICAL_TOL_PCT = assume("Supply-day typicality tolerance", 3, "A",
                         "Max % gap between a candidate's total peak buses and the median eligible day", "SUPPLY_DATE", "16 Jun shown below")
cand = eligible.loc[(eligible.dow == ref.dow) & (eligible.Fecha <= supply.FechaSer.max()), "Fecha"]
s = supply[supply.FechaSer.isin(set(cand))]
peak_by_day = s.groupby(["FechaSer", "Linea"]).NumCCReal.max().unstack()          # day x line
riders_day = riders[riders.Fecha.isin(set(cand))].groupby("Fecha").TotalViajeros.sum()
typ = pd.DataFrame({"sum_line_peaks": peak_by_day.sum(axis=1), "lines_running": peak_by_day.notna().sum(axis=1),
                    "riders": riders_day})
typ["peaks_vs_median_pct"] = (typ.sum_line_peaks / typ.sum_line_peaks.median() - 1) * 100
typ["riders_vs_median_pct"] = (typ.riders / typ.riders.median() - 1) * 100
typ["typical"] = typ.peaks_vs_median_pct.abs() <= TYPICAL_TOL_PCT
display(typ.round(1).tail(8))

calendar_only = typ.index[-1]                                   # latest candidate by the calendar rule alone
SUPPLY_DATE = assume("Supply-data day for peak_buses", typ.index[typ.typical][-1], "D",
                     "Latest same-weekday eligible day in the supply data within the typicality tolerance (brief: closest equivalent weekday)",
                     "File 2 peak_buses", f"Calendar-only day {calendar_only}")
print(f"GTFS snapshot valid {gtfs_start.date()} to {gtfs_end.date()} | supply data ends {supply.FechaSer.max()}")
print(f"Reference day: {REF_DATE} ({ref.date.day_name()}) | supply day: {SUPPLY_DATE} | calendar-only supply day: {calendar_only}")

# The calendar week around each chosen day.
for d in (REF_DATE, SUPPLY_DATE):
    w = cal[cal.week == cal.loc[cal.Fecha == d, "week"].iloc[0]]
    display(w[["Fecha", "DiaSemana", "TipoDiaEs", "TemporadaTG"]].set_index("Fecha").T)

Checks on the chosen days. GTFS must run its working-day service on the reference day, the supply day must be typical line by line, and both days must cover the same lines (lines missing from the supply data get a proxy in §4).

In [8]:

3 · Fleet baseline at 31 Dec 2025 and 2021–25 pace¶

Rebuild the fleet in service at 31 Dec 2020 and 31 Dec 2025 from the fleet register (each vehicle's start and end dates), by fuel and size; reconcile the 2025 total against EMT's and the city's published figures; print the CNG age profile, which drives retirements in File 4.

Decision record · 2025 baseline (16–18 Nov 2026) | Source | Total | Battery / hydrogen / CNG | Verdict | |---|---|---|---| | Fleet register, rebuilt here (vehicle by vehicle) | 2,210 | 452 / 10 / 1,748 | Chosen: reproducible, gives the fuel and size split, and its total matches the city's official figure exactly | | City of Madrid, Carta de Servicios 2026 (data at 31 Dec 2025) | 2,210 | not given | Confirms the total | | Comunidad de Madrid budget release, 3 Dec 2025 | 2,215 | 79% gas, >20% electric or hydrogen | Earlier date, rounded shares: noted only | | EMT, Principales cifras web page (31 Dec 2025) | 2,150 | not given | Lower than both official totals; likely a different count (e.g. buses in service). Noted, not used | | EMT 2025 accounts (press summary, 25 Mar 2026) | 2,239 implied | 456 / 10 / 1,773 | No published total matches its sum: run as a sensitivity |

Conflicting records. Five 2012 Tempus buses (9301–9305) appear as both CNG and electric with identical dates; they count as CNG (not zero-emission), which gives 76 zero-emission buses at 31 Dec 2020. Counting them as electric (81) is shown as a sensitivity: the year of full conversion does not move.

No plug-in CNG hybrids or other fuel codes are in service at 31 Dec 2025, so n_bev + n_h2 + n_cng = fleet_total holds without a counting rule. The register's newest entry is 5 Jun 2025; the matching city total suggests no material gap, but the four-bus electric difference with EMT's accounts is reported below.

In [9]:
# Rebuild the fleet in service on a date from the fleet register: the record(s) valid on that date, one row per vehicle.
reg = fleet_hist.drop_duplicates().copy()
reg["start"] = pd.to_datetime(reg.dateIni.str[:10])
reg["end"] = pd.to_datetime(reg.dateEnd.str[:10].replace("9999-12-31", "2262-04-11"))   # open-ended = still in service
first_in_service = reg.groupby("vehicleId").start.min()

FUEL_CLASS = assume("Fuel classes for the baseline", {"EL": "n_bev", "H": "n_h2", "GN": "n_cng"}, "A",
                    "Fleet register codes: EL battery-electric, H hydrogen fuel cell, GN compressed natural gas", "Files 1, 4")
ZE_CODES = {"EL", "H"}
CONFLICT_RULE = assume("Vehicle with conflicting fuel codes on the same date", "count as not zero-emission", "A",
                       "Conservative: a bus counts as zero-emission only if every record valid on the date says EL or H "
                       "(2012 Tempus buses 9301-9305 carry both GN 'TEMPUS GNC' and EL 'TEMPUS EL' records with identical dates)",
                       "ZE_2020, S0 pace", "Counted as electric: see the pace sensitivity below")

def fleet_at(date):
    """Vehicles in service on `date`, one row per vehicle, with age since first entry and size (code 02 = articulated, section 4)."""
    d = pd.Timestamp(date)
    a = reg[(reg.start <= d) & (reg.end > d)].copy()
    a["conflict"] = a.groupby("vehicleId").fuelType.transform("nunique") > 1
    a["ze_record"] = a.fuelType.isin(ZE_CODES)
    a = a.sort_values(["ze_record", "start"]).drop_duplicates("vehicleId", keep="first")   # non-zero-emission record wins a conflict
    a["age_years"] = (d - a.vehicleId.map(first_in_service)).dt.days / 365.25
    a["size"] = np.where(a.typeCapacity == "02", "Articulated", "Standard")
    return a.drop(columns="ze_record")

f20, f25 = fleet_at("2020-12-31"), fleet_at("2025-12-31")
mix = pd.DataFrame({"31 Dec 2020": f20.fuelType.value_counts(), "31 Dec 2025": f25.fuelType.value_counts()}).fillna(0).astype(int)
mix.loc["total"] = mix.sum()
display(mix)
display(pd.crosstab(f25.fuelType, f25["size"], margins=True, margins_name="total"))
check("2025 fleet: only battery-electric, hydrogen and CNG buses in service", set(f25.fuelType) <= set(FUEL_CLASS),

print("Codes in service at 31 Dec 2020 that are neither zero-emission nor CNG:",
      f20.loc[~f20.fuelType.isin(list(FUEL_CLASS)), "fuelType"].value_counts().to_dict())

4 · Line model (File 2 metrics)¶

Every EMT line with ≥1 trip on the reference day stays in File 2, including night, airport and university lines. Public line codes (C1, N26) come from GTFS route_short_name; GTFS route_id (068) is the key that joins GTFS, supply and ridership.

Daily km — method B (primary). EMT publishes each line's route as a KML file per direction and date. daily_km = Σ over directions (KML route length × trips run in that direction on the reference day). Lengths are measured on the route geometry with the haversine formula. Method A (validation only). The same km from GTFS: each trip's shape_dist_traveled (metres), summed once per trip. GTFS trips are already individual timed runs chained in vehicle blocks, so frequencies.txt is not expanded (that would double count about 26×). Lines where A and B disagree are listed; KML is used in File 2 unless a line has no KML for a direction it runs.

Decision record · daily km (team decision, 16 Nov 2026) | Option | Verdict | Why | |---|---|---| | B · KML route length × trips per direction | Chosen for File 2 | EMT's published route geometry, a source the brief lists for route length; one length per line and direction | | A · GTFS shape_dist_traveled per trip | Kept as validation | Independent check on the same day: agrees within 0.7 % city-wide | | Expand frequencies.txt headway rows | Rejected | Trips are already individual timed runs; expanding gives 8.8 M km/day instead of 0.34 M (double counting, brief §4.1) | | KML distancia field instead of geometry | Rejected | Field is a cumulative position along the route, not a segment length; geometry matches GTFS (line 1: 8.92 vs 8.82 km) |

In [13]:
# Method B: KML route length per line and direction on REF_DATE (EMT open API, no key needed).
import time, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
KML_NS = "{http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2}"
KML_DIR = os.path.join(RAW, "emt_kml", REF_DATE)
os.makedirs(KML_DIR, exist_ok=True)
KML_URL = "https://openapi.emtmadrid.es/v1/bus/kml/{date}/{line}/{direction}/3"      # type 3 = route geometry

def kml_route_km(route_id, direction):
    """Length in km of EMT's published route for a line (GTFS route_id) and direction (1 = ida, 2 = vuelta); NaN if none."""
    path = os.path.join(KML_DIR, f"L{route_id}_D{direction}.kml")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        url = KML_URL.format(date=pd.Timestamp(REF_DATE).strftime("%d-%m-%Y"), line=int(route_id), direction=direction)
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
        time.sleep(0.1)
        if r.status_code != 200 or b"<coordinates>" not in r.content:
            return np.nan
        with open(path, "wb") as f:
            f.write(r.content)
    km = 0.0
    for ls in ET.parse(path).getroot().iter(f"{KML_NS}LineString"):
        xy = np.array([[float(v) for v in pt.split(",")[:2]] for pt in ls.find(f"{KML_NS}coordinates").text.split()])
        km += haversine_km(xy[:-1, 1], xy[:-1, 0], xy[1:, 1], xy[1:, 0]).sum()
    return km

trips_dir = ref_trips.groupby(["route_id", "direction_id"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)   # trips per line and direction
kml = pd.DataFrame({d: [kml_route_km(r, d) for r in trips_dir.index] for d in (1, 2)}, index=trips_dir.index)

files = sorted(os.listdir(KML_DIR))
blob = b"".join(open(os.path.join(KML_DIR, f), "rb").read() for f in files)

Method A and the direction match. GTFS gives each trip's length; the median per line and direction is the GTFS route length. KML direction 1/2 is matched to GTFS direction_id 0/1 line by line, choosing the pairing whose lengths agree best (both directions are often similar, so the choice rarely changes km). Lines missing a KML direction they run fall back to method A.

In [14]:
# Method A: GTFS km per trip from shape_dist_traveled (metres; line 1 = 8.8 km per trip), once per trip.
feed_km = read_gtfs(PATHS["emt_gtfs.zip"], tables=("trips", "stop_times", "shapes"))
DIST_UNIT_M = assume("GTFS shape_dist_traveled unit", "metres", "D", "Line 1 trips = 8.8 km, matching its 8.9 km KML route")
trip_len = trip_km(feed_km, set(ref_trips.trip_id), dist_unit_m=True).rename("km")
t = ref_trips.join(trip_len, on="trip_id")
gtfs_len = t.groupby(["route_id", "direction_id"]).km.median().unstack()            # GTFS route length per direction
daily_km_A = t.groupby("route_id").km.sum()

# Match KML direction 1/2 to GTFS 0/1 per line.
same = (kml[1] - gtfs_len["0"]).abs().fillna(0) + (kml[2] - gtfs_len["1"]).abs().fillna(0)
swap = (kml[1] - gtfs_len["1"]).abs().fillna(0) + (kml[2] - gtfs_len["0"]).abs().fillna(0)
len0 = np.where(swap < same, kml[2], kml[1])
len1 = np.where(swap < same, kml[1], kml[2])
km_B = pd.Series(trips_dir.get("0", 0) * len0 + trips_dir.get("1", 0) * len1, index=trips_dir.index)
missing_B = (trips_dir.get("0", 0).gt(0) & pd.isna(len0)) | (trips_dir.get("1", 0).gt(0) & pd.isna(len1))

daily_km = km_B.where(~missing_B, daily_km_A)
km_source = pd.Series(np.where(missing_B, "GTFS (method A)", "KML (method B)"), index=daily_km.index)
cmp = pd.DataFrame({"line": routes.route_short_name.reindex(daily_km.index), "km_B_kml": km_B, "km_A_gtfs": daily_km_A,
                    "diff_pct": (km_B / daily_km_A - 1) * 100, "source": km_source})
print(f"Daily km on {REF_DATE}: method B {km_B.sum():,.0f} | method A {daily_km_A.sum():,.0f} | File 2 uses {daily_km.sum():,.0f}")
print("Lines falling back to method A:", list(cmp.loc[missing_B, "line"]) or "none")
display(cmp.dropna().reindex(cmp.diff_pct.abs().sort_values(ascending=False).index).head(10).round(1))
check("Daily km: methods A and B agree within 3% city-wide", abs(km_B[~missing_B].sum() / daily_km_A[~missing_B].sum() - 1) <= 0.03,
      f"{(km_B[~missing_B].sum() / daily_km_A[~missing_B].sum() - 1) * 100:+.1f}%")
check("Daily km: most lines agree within 5%", (cmp.diff_pct.abs() <= 5).mean() >= 0.9,
      f"{(cmp.diff_pct.abs() <= 5).mean():.0%} of lines")
check("Daily km: every reference-day line has a value", daily_km.notna().all() and len(daily_km) == len(ref_lines))

Peak buses. peak_buses = maximum buses in service across the hour bands on the supply day, from the official supply data only (brief File 2). Bus type per line — evidence first (alternative A). EMT does not publish bus type by line, so we start from what is evidenced and fill the rest with a proxy:

  1. How many articulated buses exist. In the fleet history, size code 02 is the only one whose models are articulated (…-ART, 118–122 places); codes 03, 04, 06 are midi and mini buses, counted as Standard (the brief has only two types). This fixes the articulated share of the 31 Dec 2025 fleet.
  2. Which lines are evidenced. Line 34 runs articulated buses: the brief cites EMT's tender for 120 electric buses as linking articulated vehicles, line 34 and Carabanchel, and the 30 articulated Solaris Urbino 18 from that tender go to Carabanchel (electrive, 31 Mar 2026).
  3. Proxy for the rest. The remaining articulated buses go to the lines with the most riders per peak bus on the supply day (articulated buses are deployed where demand per vehicle is highest) until the articulated share of peak buses matches the fleet's. Labelled P.

Decision record · bus type (team decision, 16 Nov 2026) | Option | Verdict | Why | |---|---|---| | A · Evidence first (fleet size codes + line 34), proxy for the rest | Chosen | Uses every published fact before any assumption; articulated share fixed by the fleet history | | B · Bracket low / base / high | Kept as variance check | Shows the proxy barely matters: energy −1.1 % / +1.5 %, no charging strategy changes | | All Standard | Rejected | Ignores 85 articulated buses in the 2025 fleet | | Assign by depot (e.g. all Carabanchel lines articulated) | Rejected for now | Depot allocation is not done yet (§5); revisit if B finds a depot-level source |

riders_sup = riders[riders.Fecha == SUPPLY_DATE].groupby("Linea").TotalViajeros.sum()
lines["riders_per_peak_bus"] = (riders_sup.reindex(lines.index) / lines.peak_buses).round(0)

def articulated_lines(target):
    """Evidenced lines first, then lines by riders per peak bus until articulated peak buses reach `target`."""
    chosen, n = list(EVIDENCED_ART), lines.loc[EVIDENCED_ART, "peak_buses"].sum()
    for rid in lines.drop(index=EVIDENCED_ART).riders_per_peak_bus.dropna().sort_values(ascending=False).index:
        if n + lines.at[rid, "peak_buses"] > target:
            continue
        chosen.append(rid); n += lines.at[rid, "peak_buses"]
    return chosen

ART_BASE = articulated_lines(art_target)
lines["bus_type"] = np.where(lines.index.isin(ART_BASE), "Articulated", "Standard")

File 2 formulas (brief Rule 2 and File 2 definitions). km per bus-day, energy per bus-day, the charging strategy and annual CO₂ avoided, all from P.

Charging strategy above range. Rule 2 fixes Depot (km per bus-day within 300 km Standard / 240 km Articulated) and leaves Opportunity vs Not_feasible to the team. Our rule is about energy: a bus above range must get the difference, top-up = (km per bus-day − range) × kWh/km, from daytime charging. While that top-up is at most one more battery's worth of driving (km per bus-day ≤ 2 × range), terminus or mid-day depot charging can plausibly supply it: Opportunity. Beyond that, the bus would need more energy during the day than it gets overnight, which is a fleet-size problem rather than a charging one: Not_feasible (more buses on the line, not more chargers).

Decision record · Opportunity vs Not_feasible above range (18 Nov 2026) | Option | Verdict | Why | |---|---|---| | Energy rule: Opportunity if km per bus-day ≤ 2 × range, else Not_feasible | Chosen | Uses only fixed brief parameters plus one labelled multiplier; reproducible; the top-up energy it reports sizes terminus chargers in §6 / §8 | | Same rule with 1.5 × range | Kept as sensitivity | Stricter; shows which lines flip (next cells) | | Dwell-time rule (top-up must fit in scheduled terminus layovers) | Rejected for now | EMT's GTFS leaves almost no time between a bus's trips (median 0.2 min, below), so layovers are not visible in the timetable; recovery time is likely inside trip times. Revisit if EMT publishes layovers or a charger location list | | Every above-range line Not_feasible | Rejected | Hides the daytime top-up need from the capex, though a charger can close a small gap | | Every above-range line Opportunity | Rejected | No limit: a line needing several batteries a day is not solved by a charger |

Opportunity is screening-level: whether each terminus has space, grid and timetable slack for a charger remains to be studied before investment (brief, power-assessment protocol item 4).

In [17]:
OPP_MAX_RANGE_MULT = assume("Opportunity limit: max km per bus-day as a multiple of range", 2.0, "A",
                            "Top-up at most one extra battery of driving a day; above that the line needs more buses, not chargers",
                            "File 2 charging_strategy", "1.5 x range (next cells)")

def line_metrics(lines, opp_mult=OPP_MAX_RANGE_MULT):
    """lines: DataFrame with line_id, daily_km, peak_buses, bus_type. Applies the brief's fixed formulas and our above-range rule."""
    df = lines.copy()
    rng, kwh = df.bus_type.map(P["range_km"]), df.bus_type.map(P["kwh_km"])
    df["km_per_bus_day"] = df.daily_km / df.peak_buses
    df["energy_kwh_bus_day"] = df.km_per_bus_day * kwh
    df["charging_strategy"] = np.select([df.km_per_bus_day <= rng, df.km_per_bus_day <= opp_mult * rng],
                                        ["Depot", "Opportunity"], "Not_feasible")
    df["topup_kwh_bus_day"] = (df.km_per_bus_day - rng).clip(lower=0) * kwh      # battery energy needed during the day
    cng_kg_co2_km = df.bus_type.map(P["cng_kg_km"]) * P["cng_kgco2_per_kg"]
    ele_kg_co2_km = kwh / P["charge_eff"] * P["grid_gco2_kwh"] / 1000
    df["co2_avoided_t_year"] = df.daily_km * P["service_days"] * (cng_kg_co2_km - ele_kg_co2_km) / 1000
    return df
print(f"line_metrics() ready: Depot within range, Opportunity up to {OPP_MAX_RANGE_MULT:g} x range, Not_feasible beyond")

line_metrics() ready: Depot within range, Opportunity up to 2 x range, Not_feasible beyond

Bracket (alternative B): how much does the bus-type proxy matter? The same line model run three ways: low = only the evidenced line 34 articulated; base = the evidence-first assignment above; high = articulated buses on twice as many peak buses, following the same ranking. If charging strategies and energy barely move, the proxy does not drive the conclusions.

def bracket_case(name, art):
    m = line_metrics(lines.assign(bus_type=np.where(lines.index.isin(art), "Articulated", "Standard")))
    return m, dict(case=name, articulated_lines=len(art), articulated_peak_buses=int(m.loc[art, "peak_buses"].sum()),
                   night_energy_mwh=(m.peak_buses * m.energy_kwh_bus_day).sum() / 1000,
                   lines_above_range=int((m.charging_strategy != "Depot").sum()), co2_avoided_kt=m.co2_avoided_t_year.sum() / 1000)

Data-quality flags on the File 2 inputs (ML I study guide: IQR rule, isolation forest). Two detectors, one per variable and one across variables:

  • IQR rule on each input: below Q1 − 1.5·IQR or above Q3 + 1.5·IQR.
  • Isolation forest on all inputs together, after a log transform (the inputs are right-skewed) and standardisation (so km and buses weigh the same).

Flags are for review only: no line is deleted or changed, because every line active on the reference day must stay in File 2 and large lines are real. Missing riders (lines without ridership records) are filled with the median for the detector only.

In [21]:
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
FLAG_COLS = ["daily_km", "peak_buses", "km_per_bus_day", "riders_per_peak_bus"]
IQR_K = assume("IQR fence multiplier", 1.5, "A", "Tukey fence (ML I study guide)", "Review flags only")
ISO_SHARE = assume("Isolation forest expected outlier share", 0.05, "A", "About 12 of 234 lines sent to review", "Review flags only")

X = line_table[FLAG_COLS]
def iqr_flag(s):
    q1, q3 = s.quantile([0.25, 0.75])
    return (s < q1 - IQR_K * (q3 - q1)) | (s > q3 + IQR_K * (q3 - q1))
iqr = pd.DataFrame({c: iqr_flag(X[c]) for c in FLAG_COLS})
Z = np.log1p(X.fillna(X.median()))                       # log: right-skewed inputs
Z = (Z - Z.mean()) / Z.std()                             # standardise: mean 0, SD 1
line_table["iqr_flags"] = iqr.apply(lambda r: ", ".join(c for c in FLAG_COLS if r[c]), axis=1)
line_table["iso_outlier"] = IsolationForest(n_estimators=300, contamination=ISO_SHARE, random_state=0).fit(Z).predict(Z) == -1

review = line_table[(line_table.iqr_flags != "") | line_table.iso_outlier]
print(f"Lines flagged for review: {len(review)} of {len(line_table)} (IQR: {(line_table.iqr_flags != '').sum()}, isolation forest: {line_table.iso_outlier.sum()})")
display(review[["line_id"] + FLAG_COLS + ["iqr_flags", "iso_outlier"]].round(1).sort_values("km_per_bus_day", ascending=False))

# Known cause to check: university lines have June peak buses (exam period) but November km (full term).
UNIVERSITY = ["A", "E", "F", "G", "H", "U"]
uni = line_table.index[line_table.line_id.isin(UNIVERSITY)]
print("University lines, peak buses on each eligible supply-data Tuesday (term vs June):")
display(peak_by_day[[r for r in uni if r in peak_by_day.columns]].rename(columns=line_table.line_id).tail(10))
check("Outlier review: no line removed", len(line_table) == len(lines))

Sensitivity · university lines' supply day. On 9 Jun the six university lines (A, E, F, G, H, U) run about half their term-time buses, while their km comes from a November term day.

Decision record · university lines (team decision, 16 Nov 2026) | Option | Verdict | Why | |---|---|---| | (a) 9 Jun for every line | Rejected as the only view | Simplest, but leaves the June/November mismatch unexamined | | (b) Term-time Tuesday for the six lines in File 2 | Rejected for File 2 | Mixes two supply days in one file; harder to defend as "the closest equivalent weekday" | | (c) 9 Jun in File 2, term-time day as a sensitivity | Chosen | File 2 follows one rule for every line; the report shows how much the mismatch matters |

The term-time day is picked by rule: the latest eligible Tuesday on which the university lines' total peak buses is within the typicality tolerance of their median across eligible days.

Per-bus sensitivity (Rule 2). km_per_bus_day is an average; some buses run much longer days. Each GTFS vehicle block (block_id) is one bus's planned day on the reference day, so summing its trips' km gives km per bus. A line can be Depot on average yet have buses that exceed range: those buses need a daytime top-up or a mid-day swap. This is a sensitivity; File 2 keeps the brief's line-average screening.

Block km uses GTFS trip lengths (method A), the only per-trip source; at city level it is within 1 % of the KML km used in File 2. Deadheading to and from the depot is not in the timetable, so these are in-service km: the true bus-day is somewhat longer.

Decision record · day-to-day range (team decision, 16 Nov 2026) | Option | Verdict | Pros | Cons | |---|---|---|---| | Vehicle blocks (GTFS block_id) | Chosen | EMT's own planned bus days; already in the data; matches peak buses (2,106 blocks vs 2,032, r = 0.98); finds 74 buses (3.5 %) over their range on 26 lines, 19 of which pass on the line average (44 buses); counts buses needing a midday charge or swap | Planned, not operated (mid-day swaps make real days shorter); excludes depot deadheading; no interlining visible | | First-to-last-trip span × average speed (brief's example) | Rejected | Simple, brief-suggested | Assumes one bus works the whole span, so it overstates | | Daily km ÷ off-peak buses | Rejected | Uses the official supply data | Ignores how buses are actually scheduled |

blk["range_km"] = blk.bus_type.map(P["range_km"])
blk["over_range"] = blk.block_km > blk.range_km

  • A-5 / M-30 closure, 10 Nov – 23 Dec 2026: EMT reinforced its most affected lines (Ayuntamiento). The page blocks automated reads, so the dates come from the team brief and the reinforced lines are not yet identified.
  • Metro L10 Nuevos Ministerios – Cuzco closed, 28 Mar – end of 2026, replaced by a free EMT bus from Plaza de Castilla with ten vehicles every 3–5 minutes (elDiario.es, 6 Mar 2026).
  • EMT special services running that day: route names starting SE, S + digit, or SC.

Decision D7 (team, 23 Nov 2026): keep Tue 17 Nov 2026 and document it. The A-5 / M-30 window covers the day, so the check below prints FAIL on purpose; special services are a small share of the network, and the alternative day is printed.

5 · Depot allocation and fleet reconciliation¶

Each line gets one primary depot by a transparent rule, with a capacity check, compared with three alternatives and the 2021 per-depot counts. Active buses at a depot are the sum of its lines' peak buses (this is File 3's buses_assigned, never inflated by reserves). The physical fleet per depot is reconciled to the 2,210-bus baseline with a reserve ratio r: Fleet_d = Active_d / (1 − r) (brief 4.2, steps 1–5).

Decision record · depot allocation (18–23 Nov 2026) | Option | Verdict | Why | |---|---|---| | Nearest terminal + capacity check | Chosen | Buses start and end their day at a terminal, so the closest terminal is the natural pull-out point. Pure nearest piles 637 active buses on central La Elipa (2021: 314) and leaves Sanchinarro 124, so a capacity check moves the lines with the cheapest alternative until no depot is more than 10 % above its 2021 size scaled to today's fleet | | A · Nearest terminal, no capacity check | Rejected, shown | Ignores depot size; La Elipa would need twice its 2021 fleet | | B · Nearest line centre + capacity check | Kept as sensitivity | Uses where the line runs, not where buses start; moves 69 lines | | C · La Elipa closed | Kept as sensitivity | La Elipa has had no activity since early 2022 and is being rebuilt as an all-electric depot for 318 buses (works awarded to OHLA–Seranco for €112.1 M, up to 32 months, so ready mid-2029 at best). File 3 must model it and the plan runs to 2030, so it is in the base case at its new capacity; C shows the network if it is not back in time | | Fractional (multi-depot) allocation | Not used | The brief allows one dominant depot; lines whose two nearest depots are within 1 km are listed as "either is plausible" | | Las Tablas | Excluded | Announced site (≈620 buses), not an operating 2025 depot (brief 4.2); for File 4 scenarios only |

Distances are straight-line km from GTFS terminal stops to the depot point; deadheading is a sensitivity below (straight line × 1.3).

Allocation rule and reconciliation. Primary rule, the depot summary against the 2021 counts, and the reserve-ratio reconciliation of active versus physical fleet. The capacity limit is each depot's 2021 share of buses applied to the 2025 fleet, plus 10 %: a prior, not a hard limit (brief 4.2). La Elipa uses its published new capacity, 318 buses.

In [26]:
HIST_2021 = pd.DataFrame({"depot_name": ["Carabanchel", "Fuencarral", "La Elipa", "Entrevías", "Sanchinarro"],
                          "buses_2021": [458, 486, 314, 399, 438], "lines_2021": [51, 41, 36, 42, 49]})
assume("Buses and lines per depot, 2021", HIST_2021.set_index("depot_name").to_dict("index"), "V",
       "EMT Resumen Ejecutivo 2021, 'Infraestructuras', p. 26 (brief 4.2); historical prior, not a 2025 count", "§5 capacity check")

# Where each line starts and ends: first and last stop of every reference-day trip.
with zipfile.ZipFile(PATHS["emt_gtfs.zip"]) as z:
    stops = pd.read_csv(z.open("stops.txt"), dtype=str, usecols=["stop_id", "stop_lat", "stop_lon"]).astype({"stop_lat": float, "stop_lon": float})
    st5 = pd.read_csv(z.open("stop_times.txt"), dtype=str, usecols=["trip_id", "stop_id", "stop_sequence"])
st5 = (st5[st5.trip_id.isin(t.trip_id)].assign(seq=lambda d: d.stop_sequence.astype(int)).sort_values(["trip_id", "seq"])
       .merge(t[["trip_id", "route_id"]], on="trip_id").merge(stops, on="stop_id"))
ends = pd.concat([st5.groupby("trip_id").head(1), st5.groupby("trip_id").tail(1)]).drop_duplicates(["route_id", "stop_id"])
mids = st5.drop_duplicates(["route_id", "stop_id"]).groupby("route_id")[["stop_lat", "stop_lon"]].mean()

def depot_km(points, by_route=True):
    """Straight-line km from each line to each depot: the closest of its terminals (or its stop centroid)."""
    out = pd.DataFrame({d.depot_name: haversine_km(points.stop_lat, points.stop_lon, d.latitude, d.longitude)
                        for _, d in DEPOTS.iterrows()}, index=points.index)
    return (out.join(points[["route_id"]]).groupby("route_id").min() if by_route else out).reindex(lines.index)

DIST = depot_km(ends)                        # primary: nearest terminal
DIST_MID = depot_km(mids, by_route=False)    # alternative: centre of the line

RESERVE_R = assume("Reserve ratio r: share of the fleet not on the road at the network peak",
                   round(1 - lines.peak_buses.sum() / BASELINE_2025["fleet_total"], 4), "D",
                   f"1 - {int(lines.peak_buses.sum())} peak buses (File 2) / {BASELINE_2025['fleet_total']} buses (§3 baseline); same r at every depot",
                   "§5 fleet per depot (not File 3)", "Depot-specific r from 2021 shares")
CAP_TOL = assume("Depot capacity check: allowed excess over the 2021 size scaled to the 2025 fleet", 0.10, "A",
                 "2021 counts are a prior, not a limit (brief 4.2); 10 % absorbs growth and re-planning since 2021", "§5", "0 % and 20 %")

CAP_OVERRIDE = {"La Elipa": assume("La Elipa capacity after rebuilding (buses)", 318, "V",
                                    "EMT construction tender for the new La Elipa operations centre, June 2026: 318 places for electric "
                                    "buses (inactive since early 2022)", "§5 capacity check, §6")}

def capacity(depots=None, tol=CAP_TOL):
    """2021 share of buses applied to the 2025 fleet, plus tol; a depot with a newer published capacity uses that instead."""
    h = HIST_2021.set_index("depot_name").buses_2021
    h = h if depots is None else h[depots]
    cap = h / h.sum() * BASELINE_2025["fleet_total"] * (1 + tol)
    for d, v in CAP_OVERRIDE.items():
        if d in cap.index:
            cap[d] = v
    return cap

def allocate(dist, cap=None):
    """Nearest depot; then, while a depot's fleet (active / (1 - r)) exceeds its capacity, move the line whose
    next-best depot with room adds the fewest km. Returns a Series route_id -> depot."""
    dep = dist.idxmin(axis=1)
    if cap is None:
        return dep
    need = lines.peak_buses / (1 - RESERVE_R)
    for _ in range(len(dep)):
        fleet = need.groupby(dep).sum().reindex(cap.index, fill_value=0)
        over = fleet - cap
        if (over <= 0).all():
            break
        d0, best = over.idxmax(), None
        for rid in dep.index[dep == d0]:
            for alt in cap.index:
                if alt != d0 and fleet[alt] + need[rid] <= cap[alt]:
                    extra = dist.at[rid, alt] - dist.at[rid, d0]
                    if best is None or extra < best[0]:
                        best = (extra, rid, alt)
        if best is None:
            break
        dep[best[1]] = best[2]
    return dep

CAP = capacity()
DEPOT_OF = allocate(DIST, CAP)
line_table["depot_name"] = DEPOT_OF
lines["depot_name"] = DEPOT_OF

def depot_summary(dep):
    s = pd.DataFrame({"lines": dep.value_counts(), "active_buses": lines.peak_buses.groupby(dep).sum()}).reindex(HIST_2021.depot_name).fillna(0).astype(int)
    raw = s.active_buses / (1 - RESERVE_R)
    fl = np.floor(raw).astype(int)                       # largest-remainder rounding so the total is exactly the baseline fleet
    fl[(raw - fl).sort_values(ascending=False).index[:BASELINE_2025["fleet_total"] - fl.sum()]] += 1
    s["fleet_est"] = fl
    return s

SUMMARY = depot_summary(DEPOT_OF).join(HIST_2021.set_index("depot_name"))
SUMMARY["capacity_check"] = CAP.round(0).astype(int)
SUMMARY["fleet_vs_2021_pct"] = ((SUMMARY.fleet_est / SUMMARY.buses_2021 - 1) * 100).round(1)
SUMMARY.loc["total"] = SUMMARY.sum(numeric_only=True)
SUMMARY.loc["total", "fleet_vs_2021_pct"] = round((SUMMARY.at["total", "fleet_est"] / SUMMARY.at["total", "buses_2021"] - 1) * 100, 1)
display(SUMMARY)

pure = allocate(DIST)
moved = (DEPOT_OF != pure)
km_line = pd.Series({rid: DIST.at[rid, DEPOT_OF[rid]] for rid in DIST.index})
margin = DIST.apply(lambda r: r.nsmallest(2).diff().iloc[-1], axis=1)
print(f"Moved by the capacity check: {moved.sum()} lines, {int(lines.peak_buses[moved].sum())} peak buses "
      f"({list(lines.loc[moved, 'line_id'])[:15]}{'…' if moved.sum() > 15 else ''})")
print(f"Terminal-to-depot distance, assigned depot: median {km_line.median():.1f} km, max {km_line.max():.1f} km (line {lines.line_id[km_line.idxmax()]})")
print(f"Lines whose two nearest depots are within 1 km of each other (either is plausible): {(margin < 1).sum()}")

check("Every line has exactly one primary depot", DEPOT_OF.notna().all() and DEPOT_OF.index.equals(lines.index))

Alternatives. The same summary under rules A–C. A depot whose active buses move a lot between rules is one where the allocation, and therefore its readiness in §6, is uncertain. The depots come in close pairs (Fuencarral–Sanchinarro 3 km apart, Carabanchel–Entrevías 4 km), so for many lines the two nearest depots are within 1 km of each other: within a pair the split is weakly determined, while the split between north, east and south is robust. This is also why Sanchinarro ends below its 2021 size: Fuencarral wins most near-ties.

Sensitivity · deadheading and the reserve ratio. Buses also drive empty from the depot to the line and back. With §5's terminal-to-depot distances (straight line × 1.3 road factor, A), how many vehicle blocks go over range? File 2 keeps the brief's definition (service km only); the count goes to §8's list of what capex leaves out. The reserve ratio r is also reconciled with notebook 04, which divides the same spare buses by peak buses instead of by the fleet.

# Deadheading sensitivity (§4 follow-up): a bus also drives from its depot to the line and back each day.
DETOUR = assume("Road distance / straight-line distance for deadheading", 1.3, "A",
                "Round urban detour factor; straight-line km from each line's nearest terminal to its assigned depot (§5)",
                "§5 sensitivity; §8 lists the over-range buses as a capex exclusion", "1.0 and 1.5")
dh_km = 2 * DETOUR * pd.Series({rid: DIST.at[rid, DEPOT_OF[rid]] for rid in DIST.index})      # out and back, per bus-day
blk["block_km_dh"] = blk.block_km + blk.route_id.map(dh_km)
blk["over_range_dh"] = blk.block_km_dh > blk.range_km
OVER_RANGE_BLOCKS, OVER_RANGE_BLOCKS_DH = int(blk.over_range.sum()), int(blk.over_range_dh.sum())
km_dh = line_table.km_per_bus_day + dh_km.reindex(line_table.index)

flip = line_table[(line_table.km_per_bus_day <= rng) & (km_dh > rng)]

Sensitivity · rail-replacement contingency. EMT also lends buses to Metro closures: the SE6 replacement for Metro Line 6 (Legazpi–Moncloa, Sep–Dec 2025) ran with 53 buses, articulated and standard (CRTM). If a contingency pool of that size is held back from the reserve, the operating reserve at each depot shrinks. Printed only; File 3 and buses_assigned are unchanged. London contracts rail replacement out instead (lessons matrix, notes/).

In [29]:
CONTINGENCY = assume("Rail-replacement contingency held back from the reserve (buses)", 0, "A",
                     "Default 0 (no pool); sensitivity uses the SE6 anchor below", "§5 sensitivity only", "SE6 size")
SE6_BUSES = assume("Buses on the SE6 Metro L6 replacement, Sep-Dec 2025", 53, "P",
                   "CRTM notice 26 Aug 2025, updated 19 Dec 2025: SE6 Legazpi-Moncloa 'con una dotacion de 53 autobuses' "
                   "(proxy for a future closure). The 60 vehicles for summer 2025 in the team brief are not on this page and are not used",
                   "§5 sensitivity")
dep = SUMMARY.loc[HIST_2021.depot_name, ["active_buses", "fleet_est"]].copy()
rows = []
for c in (CONTINGENCY, SE6_BUSES):
    held = (dep.fleet_est / dep.fleet_est.sum() * c).round(1)          # pool held in proportion to each depot's fleet
    r_op = (dep.fleet_est - dep.active_buses - held) / dep.fleet_est
    rows.append(pd.Series(r_op.round(3), name=f"reserve ratio, {c} held"))
cont = pd.concat(rows, axis=1)
cont.loc["network"] = [(dep.fleet_est.sum() - dep.active_buses.sum() - c) / dep.fleet_est.sum() for c in (CONTINGENCY, SE6_BUSES)]
display(cont.round(3))
check("Contingency pool fits inside the reserve at every depot", (cont.iloc[:, -1] > 0).all(),
      f"lowest reserve ratio with {SE6_BUSES} held: {cont.iloc[:, -1].min():.1%}")

6 · Depot energy, power and readiness (File 3)¶

night_energy_mwh = Σ peak_buses × energy_kwh_bus_day / 1000 (all assigned lines); peak_mw_unmanaged = buses × 100 kW; peak_mw_managed = energy ÷ (7 h × 0.90). Connection: Sanchinarro 8 MW main + 5 MW backup is Evidenced; other depots use a documented proxy (Estimated). Readiness per Rule 4, plus at least one alternative connection hypothesis.

Decision record · depot grid connections (23 Nov 2026) | Option | How it works | Verdict | |---|---|---| | Direct evidence | Published connection MW from a depot project | Used for Sanchinarro (8 MW main supply, works awarded Mar 2026) and La Elipa (substation up to 20 MW, new depot tendered Jun 2026); both are planned capacity, labelled Evidenced | | H1 · Charging points × kW per point | Published charging points × 61.9 kW, the connection-per-point of the two evidenced projects (28 MW / 452 points) | Base for Carabanchel, Fuencarral, Entrevías (Estimated) | | H1-low · EMT's own simultaneity | Points × 118 / 260 (EMT: 118 buses charge at once on 260 points, Carabanchel 2024) × 100 kW | Alternative hypothesis (low) | | H3/H4-high · New-build standard | Sanchinarro counts its 5 MW backup; other estimated depots get La Elipa's design ratio (20 MW / 318 buses) × their fleet | Alternative hypothesis (high): what full rebuilding would give | | H2 · Nearest grid-node capacity | UFD / e-distribución published spare capacity | Not used: node capacity is not the depot's connection (brief 4.2) and the network operator per depot is unverified |

Readiness compares the depot's managed MW for the full-depot screening case with the connection (Rule 4). It is indicative: three of five connections are proxies, and the two evidenced ones are planned, not yet built.

In [30]:
def depot_table(file2, depots):
    """depots: depot_name, latitude, longitude, connection_mw_estimate, connection_evidence."""
    g = file2.assign(e=file2.peak_buses * file2.energy_kwh_bus_day / 1000).groupby("depot_name").agg(
        n_lines_assigned=("line_id", "count"), buses_assigned=("peak_buses", "sum"),
        night_energy_mwh=("e", "sum"), conversion_year=("electrification_year", "max")).reset_index()
    d = depots.merge(g, on="depot_name", how="left")
    d["peak_mw_unmanaged"] = d.buses_assigned * P["charger_kw"] / 1000
    d["peak_mw_managed"] = d.night_energy_mwh / (P["window_h"] * P["charge_eff"])
    c = d.connection_mw_estimate
    d["readiness_status"] = np.where(d.peak_mw_managed <= c, "Ready", np.where(d.peak_mw_managed <= 1.5 * c, "Upgrade", "Critical"))
    return d
print("depot_table() ready: File 3 columns from File 2 lines and depot connections (Rule 4 readiness)")

depot_table() ready: File 3 columns from File 2 lines and depot connections (Rule 4 readiness)

Connection capacity: evidence per depot. Each figure says what it is (planned connection, charging points) and where it comes from. The network had 410 charging points at the end of 2025 (250 pantographs, 160 plugs) across Carabanchel, Fuencarral, Entrevías and Sanchinarro; the per-depot counts in service at the end of 2025 add up to that total within 10 points. Estimates use the points once announced works finish (Sanchinarro's 114 pantographs, La Elipa's rebuild).

assume("Depot charging points and planned connections", CONN_EVIDENCE[["depot_name", "points_2025", "charging_points", "planned_mw"]].to_dict("records"), "V",
       "; ".join(CONN_EVIDENCE.evidence), "§6 connection estimates")
pts_in_service = int(CONN_EVIDENCE.points_2025.sum())
check("Charging points in service at end 2025 match EMT's published 410 within 10", abs(pts_in_service - 410) <= 10,
      f"{pts_in_service} vs 410")

ev = CONN_EVIDENCE.dropna(subset=["planned_mw"])
KW_PER_POINT = assume("Connection per charging point (kW)", round(ev.planned_mw.sum() * 1000 / ev.charging_points.sum(), 1), "D",
                      "Sanchinarro 8 MW / 134 points and La Elipa 20 MW / 318 points (the two evidenced projects)", "H1 base", "H1-low, H3/H4-high")
SIMULTANEITY = assume("Share of charging points EMT runs at once", round(118 / 260, 3), "D",
                      "EMT, Mar 2024: 118 buses charge at once on Carabanchel's 260 points", "H1-low")
ELIPA_KW_PER_BUS = assume("New-build connection per bus (kW)", round(20000 / 318, 1), "D", "La Elipa design: 20 MW for 318 buses", "H3/H4-high")
SANCH_BACKUP_MW = assume("Sanchinarro backup supply (MW)", 5.0, "V", "EMT, Mar 2026 (different substation)", "H3/H4-high only; N-1 backup, not normal capacity")

ZE_2025_IDS = assume("Lines fully zero-emission at 31 Dec 2025 (line-level evidence)", ["001", "002", "22", "87", "108", "121"], "V",
                     "001/002: El Independiente 18 Feb 2026 ('operadas con una flota 100% electrica'); 22, 87, 108, 121: EMT 2 Jul 2025 "
                     "(latest lines with 'autobuses exclusivamente electricos'). EMT reports 45 such lines but publishes no list; the other 39 "
                     "cannot be identified from published sources, so they get 2026 or later (evidence gap stated in the report)",
                     "electrification_year 2025; connection floor (A3)", "39 unidentified lines get 2026+")
_mw_line = line_table.peak_buses * line_table.energy_kwh_bus_day / 1000 / (P["window_h"] * P["charge_eff"])
BASE_LOAD_MW = _mw_line[line_table.line_id.isin(ZE_2025_IDS)].groupby(line_table.depot_name).sum()
CONN_FLOOR = assume("Estimated connection floored at the load of the lines already electric in 2025 (MW, rounded up to 0.1)",
                    (np.ceil(BASE_LOAD_MW * 10) / 10).to_dict(), "P",
                    "A depot cannot have less connection than the electric lines it already runs; applies to Estimated depots, base and "
                    "low hypotheses", "connection_mw_estimate for Estimated depots (A3)")
fleet_d = SUMMARY.loc[HIST_2021.depot_name, "fleet_est"]
def connection(hyp):
    """Connection MW per depot under a hypothesis: 'base', 'low' or 'high'. Evidenced depots keep their published MW."""
    out = {}
    for r in CONN_EVIDENCE.itertuples():
        if pd.notna(r.planned_mw):
            out[r.depot_name] = r.planned_mw + (SANCH_BACKUP_MW if hyp == "high" and r.depot_name == "Sanchinarro" else 0)
        elif hyp == "base":
            out[r.depot_name] = max(r.charging_points * KW_PER_POINT / 1000, CONN_FLOOR.get(r.depot_name, 0.0))
        elif hyp == "low":
            out[r.depot_name] = max(r.charging_points * SIMULTANEITY * P["charger_kw"] / 1000, CONN_FLOOR.get(r.depot_name, 0.0))
        else:
            out[r.depot_name] = fleet_d[r.depot_name] * ELIPA_KW_PER_BUS / 1000
    return pd.Series(out).round(1)

DEPOT_CONN = DEPOTS[["depot_name", "latitude", "longitude"]].assign(
    connection_mw_estimate=lambda d: d.depot_name.map(connection("base")),
    connection_evidence=lambda d: np.where(d.depot_name.isin(ev.depot_name), "Evidenced", "Estimated"))
DEPOT_DRAFT = depot_table(line_table.assign(electrification_year=np.nan), DEPOT_CONN)   # conversion_year arrives with §7
for hyp in ("low", "high"):
    c = DEPOT_DRAFT.depot_name.map(connection(hyp))
    DEPOT_DRAFT[f"readiness_{hyp}"] = np.where(DEPOT_DRAFT.peak_mw_managed <= c, "Ready", np.where(DEPOT_DRAFT.peak_mw_managed <= 1.5 * c, "Upgrade", "Critical"))
    DEPOT_DRAFT[f"connection_{hyp}"] = c.values
DEPOT_DRAFT["managed_vs_connection"] = (DEPOT_DRAFT.peak_mw_managed / DEPOT_DRAFT.connection_mw_estimate).round(2)
display(DEPOT_DRAFT[["depot_name", "n_lines_assigned", "buses_assigned", "night_energy_mwh", "peak_mw_unmanaged", "peak_mw_managed",
                     "connection_mw_estimate", "connection_evidence", "managed_vs_connection", "readiness_status",
                     "connection_low", "readiness_low", "connection_high", "readiness_high"]].round(1))
flips = DEPOT_DRAFT[(DEPOT_DRAFT.readiness_status != DEPOT_DRAFT.readiness_low) | (DEPOT_DRAFT.readiness_status != DEPOT_DRAFT.readiness_high)]
print(f"City: {DEPOT_DRAFT.peak_mw_managed.sum():.1f} MW managed charging needed vs {DEPOT_DRAFT.connection_mw_estimate.sum():.1f} MW "
      f"connection (base); {DEPOT_DRAFT.peak_mw_unmanaged.sum():.1f} MW if every bus charged at once at 100 kW")

      {r.depot_name: f"{r.readiness_low} / {r.readiness_status} / {r.readiness_high} (low / base / high)" for r in flips.itertuples()})
check("Rule 4: readiness follows managed MW vs connection (Ready <= 1, Upgrade <= 1.5, Critical above)",
      (DEPOT_DRAFT.readiness_status == np.select([DEPOT_DRAFT.managed_vs_connection <= 1, DEPOT_DRAFT.managed_vs_connection <= 1.5],

Needed connection, sensitivities and the interim network. For each depot: the connection it would need to be Ready (managed MW) or Upgrade (managed MW ÷ 1.5), against the low / base / high hypotheses. All are planned or estimated capacity, none confirmed by the grid operator. Then two sensitivities on the base connection, a hot day (+25 % energy, A) and the network without night (N) lines, and the interim network while La Elipa is rebuilt (alternative C, §5).

In [32]:
def readiness(mw, conn):
    return np.where(mw <= conn, "Ready", np.where(mw <= 1.5 * conn, "Upgrade", "Critical"))

# Connection each depot needs to be Ready (managed MW) or Upgrade (managed MW / 1.5), against each hypothesis
need = DEPOT_DRAFT.set_index("depot_name")[["peak_mw_managed"]].rename(columns={"peak_mw_managed": "mw_for_ready"})
need["mw_for_upgrade"] = need.mw_for_ready / 1.5
for hyp in ("low", "base", "high"):
    c = connection(hyp).reindex(need.index)
    need[f"connection_{hyp}"] = c
    need[f"readiness_{hyp}"] = readiness(need.mw_for_ready, c)
    need[f"mw_short_of_ready_{hyp}"] = (need.mw_for_ready - c).clip(lower=0)
display(need.round(1))

# Sensitivities on the base connection: a hot day, and the network without night lines
HOT_DAY = assume("Hot-day energy uplift (air conditioning)", 0.25, "A",
                 "Round sensitivity; the brief's kWh/km already include average HVAC", "§6 readiness sensitivity", "+10 % and +40 %")
night = line_table.index[line_table.line_id.str.startswith("N")]
conn_base = connection("base").reindex(need.index)
no_n = depot_table(line_table.drop(index=night).assign(electrification_year=np.nan), DEPOT_CONN).set_index("depot_name")
sens6 = pd.DataFrame({"base": need.readiness_base,
                      f"hot day +{HOT_DAY:.0%}": readiness(need.mw_for_ready * (1 + HOT_DAY), conn_base),
                      f"excluding {len(night)} N lines": readiness(no_n.peak_mw_managed.reindex(need.index), conn_base)}, index=need.index)
display(sens6)

# Interim network while La Elipa is rebuilt (alternative C, §5): its lines run from the other four depots
interim = depot_table(line_table.assign(depot_name=alts["C · La Elipa closed (nearest of four + capacity)"], electrification_year=np.nan),
                      DEPOT_CONN[DEPOT_CONN.depot_name != "La Elipa"])
print("Interim, La Elipa closed until its rebuild (alternative C):")
display(interim[["depot_name", "n_lines_assigned", "buses_assigned", "night_energy_mwh", "peak_mw_managed", "connection_mw_estimate",
                 "readiness_status"]].round(1))

7 · Prioritisation (completes File 2)¶

Multi-criteria priority_rank, then electrification_year under S1 so a better rank never has a later year. Use 2025 only for lines already fully zero-emission at the baseline (the 6 lines with line-level evidence; EMT reports 45 electric lines but publishes no list).

Why the criteria are transformed and rescaled (ML I study guide). The criteria come in different units (tonnes of CO₂, riders, a category), so weighting them raw would let the largest unit dominate. Each criterion is:

  1. log-transformed if right-skewed (CO₂ avoided, riders): shrinks the long tail so a few very large lines do not swamp the rest;
  2. min-max rescaled to 0–1, so weights read directly as shares of the score;
  3. checked with a correlation filter: two criteria above |r| = 0.8 carry the same information, keep one.

Standardisation (z-score) is run as an alternative scaling; if both give nearly the same ranking, the choice of scaling does not drive the result.

Decision record · criteria (team decision, 23 Nov 2026) | Criterion | Why | Weight | |---|---|---| | CO₂ avoided (t/yr, log) | Climate impact of converting the line | 0.35 | | Riders per peak bus (log) | Demand intensity, size-free: replaces riders per day, which correlated 0.81 with CO₂ (both grow with line size) | 0.20 | | Feasibility (Depot 1, Opportunity 0.5, Not_feasible 0) | Easiest conversions first | 0.20 | | Depot readiness (Ready 1, Upgrade 0.5, Critical 0, from §6) | Lines at depots with grid headroom go first; Critical depots wait for their works | 0.25 |

Weights were set by the team on 23 Nov 2026 (label A: a judgement, not a measurement); the z-score check below tests whether the scaling choice moves the ranking (it moves it moderately: see the printed rho).

In [34]:
# Multi-criteria score; criteria and weights are a team decision (23 Nov 2026).
pr = line_table.copy()
pr["riders_per_day"] = riders_sup.reindex(pr.index)
READINESS_SCORE = {"Ready": 1.0, "Upgrade": 0.5, "Critical": 0.0}
pr["depot_readiness"] = pr.depot_name.map(DEPOT_DRAFT.set_index("depot_name").readiness_status).map(READINESS_SCORE)
pr["feasibility"] = pr.charging_strategy.map({"Depot": 1.0, "Opportunity": 0.5, "Not_feasible": 0.0})
CRITERIA = assume("Priority criteria: (log transform?, weight)", {
    "co2_avoided_t_year": (True, 0.35),     # climate impact
    "riders_per_peak_bus": (True, 0.20),    # demand intensity, size-free (riders per day correlated 0.81 with CO2)
    "feasibility": (False, 0.20),           # easiest conversions first
    "depot_readiness": (False, 0.25),       # §6: lines at depots with grid headroom first
}, "A", "Team decision, 23 Nov 2026 (judgement; scaling checked below)", "priority_rank, electrification_year", "Scaling sensitivity below")

def criterion_values(df, log):
    """Transformed criteria: log1p where flagged; missing riders filled with the median (logged as an imputation)."""
    out = {}
    for col, (use_log, _) in CRITERIA.items():
        v = df[col].fillna(df[col].median())
        out[col] = np.log1p(v) if use_log else v
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

def score(df, scaling="minmax"):
    v = criterion_values(df, log=True)
    s = (v - v.min()) / (v.max() - v.min()) if scaling == "minmax" else (v - v.mean()) / v.std()
    return sum(w * s[c] for c, (_, w) in CRITERIA.items())

print(f"Riders missing for {pr.riders_per_peak_bus.isna().sum()} lines: filled with the median for scoring only")
display(criterion_values(pr, log=True).corr().round(2))
corr = criterion_values(pr, log=True).corr().where(lambda m: ~np.eye(len(m), dtype=bool))
check("Criteria filter: no two criteria correlated above |r| = 0.8", corr.abs().max().max() <= 0.8,
      f"max |r| = {corr.abs().max().max():.2f}")

pr["score"] = score(pr, "minmax")
pr["priority_rank"] = pr.score.rank(ascending=False, method="first").astype(int)
alt_rank = score(pr, "zscore").rank(ascending=False, method="first")
rho = pr.priority_rank.corr(alt_rank, method="spearman")
print(f"Scaling sensitivity: min-max vs z-score ranking, Spearman rho = {rho:.3f} (below 0.95: the ranking moves moderately; "
      "§7 below counts how many lines change year)")
display(pr.sort_values("priority_rank")[["line_id", "priority_rank", "score", "co2_avoided_t_year", "riders_per_peak_bus",
                                         "charging_strategy", "depot_name", "depot_readiness"]].head(10).round(2))

Electrification year: a cumulative bus cap per year (B5). Lines convert best score first, but each year can only take the buses EMT can bring in: 2026 is capped at the 70 e-buses budgeted for 2026 (D3), and the rest of the conversion is spread evenly over 2027–2030, so S1 still reaches 100 % in 2030. A line takes the earliest year whose cumulative cap it still fits under. Two depot floors apply: La Elipa lines from 2030 (works awarded for €112.1 M, up to 32 months from signing, so ready mid-2029 at best) and Fuencarral lines last, in 2030 (the depot is due to close and be replaced by Las Tablas). Ranks are then sorted by (year, score), so a better rank never has a later year (Rule 3).

Lines already zero-emission at 31 Dec 2025 get 2025 only where line-level evidence exists (brief, File 2): 001 and 002 (a 100 % electric fleet, El Independiente, Feb 2026) and 22, 87, 108, 121 (lines now run exclusively with electric buses, EMT, 2 Jul 2025). EMT reports 45 fully electric lines but publishes no list, so the other 39 get 2026 or later; line 145 is described only as "using hydrogen technology", not as fully zero-emission.

Decision record · year bins (team decision, 23 Nov 2026) | Option | Verdict | Why | |---|---|---| | Cumulative bus cap; 2026 = budgeted deliveries | Chosen | Matches what EMT can receive; S1 buys the same e-buses as S0 in 2026 | | Equal number of lines per year (qcut on rank) | Dropped | Put a fifth of the network in 2026, several times the 70 buses delivered | | Depot by depot | Used as floors only | La Elipa and Fuencarral wait for their works; elsewhere the score decides |

In [35]:
# ZE_2025_IDS is set in §6 (it also floors the depot connections, A3)
ZE_2025_LINES = list(pr.index[pr.line_id.isin(ZE_2025_IDS)])
YEARS = list(range(2026, 2031))

# B5 + A2: a cumulative bus cap per year. 2026 is what EMT actually receives (D3); lines at La Elipa and Fuencarral cannot convert
# before their floor year, so they are placed there first and the rest is spread evenly over 2027-2029. S1 still reaches 100 % in 2030.
S1_DELIVERED_2026 = assume("Zero-emission buses delivered in 2026 (D3)", 70, "V",
                           "EMT 2026 budget: 70 e-buses, EUR 47.7 m (notes/financial-model.md)", "File 2 years, File 4 2026 in both scenarios")
DEPOT_EARLIEST = assume("Earliest electrification year by depot", {"La Elipa": 2030, "Fuencarral": 2030}, "P",
                        "La Elipa: works awarded to OHLA-Seranco (EUR 112.1 m), up to 32 months from signing, so mid-2029 at best and the first "
                        "full year is 2030; Fuencarral: due to close and be replaced by Las Tablas (City of Madrid), so its lines go last",
                        "electrification_year, File 3 conversion_year", "La Elipa 2029 if the works finish early")
to_convert = BASELINE_2025["fleet_total"] - BASELINE_2025["n_bev"] - BASELINE_2025["n_h2"]
share_2026 = S1_DELIVERED_2026 / to_convert
later = pr.index.difference(ZE_2025_LINES)
total_later = pr.loc[later, "peak_buses"].sum()
FREE_YEARS = [2027, 2028, 2029]

def assign_years(score_series, floors=DEPOT_EARLIEST):
    """Year per line (not 2025 lines): best score first into the earliest year whose cumulative cap still holds.
    Caps: 2026 = the delivered share; buses that cannot move before their depot's floor are reserved in that year; the rest is
    spread evenly over FREE_YEARS. Returns (year per line, cumulative caps)."""
    floor = pr.depot_name.map(floors).fillna(2026).astype(int)
    forced = pr.loc[later].groupby(floor.loc[later]).peak_buses.sum()
    cap_2026 = share_2026 * total_later
    free_per_year = (total_later - cap_2026 - forced.drop(2026, errors="ignore").sum()) / len(FREE_YEARS)
    caps, run = {}, 0.0
    for y in YEARS:
        run += cap_2026 if y == 2026 else (free_per_year if y in FREE_YEARS else 0.0) + forced.get(y, 0)
        caps[y] = run
    caps[YEARS[-1]] = total_later
    used, year_of = {y: 0.0 for y in YEARS}, {}
    for rid in score_series.loc[later].sort_values(ascending=False).index:     # best score first
        b = pr.at[rid, "peak_buses"]
        y = next(y for y in YEARS if y >= floor[rid]
                 and all(sum(used[k] for k in YEARS if k <= z) + b <= caps[z] + 1e-9 for z in YEARS if z >= y))
        year_of[rid] = y
        used[y] += b
    return pd.Series(year_of), caps

year_of, CAPS = assign_years(pr.score)
floor = pr.depot_name.map(DEPOT_EARLIEST).fillna(2026).astype(int)
pr.loc[ZE_2025_LINES, "electrification_year"] = 2025
pr.loc[later, "electrification_year"] = year_of
pr["electrification_year"] = pr.electrification_year.astype(int)
# Rank by (year, score) so a better rank never has a later year (Rule 3).
pr["priority_rank"] = pr.sort_values(["electrification_year", "score"], ascending=[True, False]).assign(r=range(1, len(pr) + 1)).r.reindex(pr.index)

per_year = pr.groupby("electrification_year").agg(lines=("line_id", "count"), peak_buses=("peak_buses", "sum"))
per_year["fleet_buses_equivalent"] = (per_year.peak_buses / total_later * to_convert).round(0)
per_depot = pd.crosstab(pr.depot_name, pr.electrification_year, values=pr.peak_buses, aggfunc="sum").fillna(0).astype(int)
display(per_year.T)
display(per_depot)
nonfloor_2030 = int(pr.loc[later][(year_of == 2030) & (floor.loc[later] < 2030)].peak_buses.sum())
free_spread = int(per_year.loc[FREE_YEARS, "peak_buses"].max() - per_year.loc[FREE_YEARS, "peak_buses"].min())
print(f"2027-2029 conversions: {per_year.loc[FREE_YEARS, 'peak_buses'].astype(int).tolist()} peak buses (spread {free_spread}); "
      f"2030 holds La Elipa and Fuencarral ({int(per_year.loc[2030, 'peak_buses'])} peak buses), the cost of waiting for the La Elipa works "
      f"and Las Tablas; buses outside a depot floor placed in 2030: {nonfloor_2030}")
_alt, _ = assign_years(pr.score, {**DEPOT_EARLIEST, "La Elipa": 2029})
print("Sensitivity (printed only), La Elipa floor 2029: peak buses per year",
      pr.loc[later].assign(y=_alt).groupby("y").peak_buses.sum().astype(int).to_dict())
_z, _ = assign_years(score(pr, "zscore"))
_moved = (_z - year_of).abs()
print(f"z-score scaling: {int((_moved > 0).sum())} of {len(later)} lines change year, {int((_moved > 1).sum())} by more than one year "
      f"(rho {rho:.3f}, §7 above)")
s = pr.sort_values("priority_rank")
check("Lines with 2025 evidence found in File 2", len(ZE_2025_LINES) == len(ZE_2025_IDS), f"{len(ZE_2025_LINES)} of {len(ZE_2025_IDS)}")
check("Rule 3: a better rank never has a later electrification_year", s.electrification_year.is_monotonic_increasing)
check("priority_rank is unique 1..N", sorted(pr.priority_rank) == list(range(1, len(pr) + 1)))
check("2026 conversions fit inside the 2026 deliveries (B5)", per_year.loc[2026, "fleet_buses_equivalent"] <= S1_DELIVERED_2026 + 1,
      f"{per_year.loc[2026, 'fleet_buses_equivalent']:.0f} fleet buses vs {S1_DELIVERED_2026} delivered")

8 · Scenarios 2026–2035 (File 4)¶

S0 – 2021–25 pace, adjusted for tenders and deliveries (report both paces). S1 – 100 % zero-emission by 31 Dec 2030, held to 2035. Explicit yearly purchases and retirements (not inferred from fleet change); service-km allocation by technology; standard/articulated km mix; grid-input energy (÷ 0.90); CNG tonnes; CO₂; avoided CO₂ vs counterfactual (2025 ZE share frozen); capex in constant 2025 €, excl. VAT. Then the earliest credible year and binding constraint, with ≥2 sensitivities.

Inputs. Each value carries its label and source; the CNG price, charger cost, bus life and S0 deliveries reuse the research in notebook 04 (Scenario Lab).

FLEET = BASELINE_2025["fleet_total"]                       # D1: 2,210 register baseline (2,239 kept as a sensitivity in notebook 04)
ZE25 = BASELINE_2025["n_bev"] + BASELINE_2025["n_h2"]
BUS_LIFE = assume("Bus service life (years), all technologies (D2)", 13, "P",
                  "EMT cut its bus amortisation period from 15 to 13 years (diario.madrid.es/?p=17529, via notebook 04)",
                  "retirements in both scenarios", "12 (financial model) and 15")
CNG_PRICE_EUR = assume("CNG bus purchase price (EUR)", 310_000, "D",
                       "EMT bought 200 gas buses for EUR 62 m in 2022 (diario.madrid.es/?p=72588, via notebook 04); one price for both sizes",
                       "S0 capex (CNG replacements before 2030)")
CHARGER_EUR = assume("Charging infrastructure per point (EUR) (D4)", 110_000, "D",
                     "Sanchinarro award: EUR 12,581,413.59 excl. VAT for 114 inverted pantographs, including the grid connection works and "
                     "canopy (EMT Mar 2026; TED 3953-2026) = EUR 110k per point; one point per battery bus (brief 4.5)",
                     "capex_meur", "EUR 57k (Carabanchel, existing grid) and EUR 203k (new substation)")
POINTS_2025 = assume("Charging points in service at end 2025", 410, "V", "EMT: 410 points (250 pantographs, 160 plugs), see §6", "charger capex")
COMMITTED = assume("Committed depot projects: (EUR m, {year: share})", {
    "Sanchinarro electrification (114 points, 8 MW)": (12.58, {2026: 0.5, 2027: 0.5}),
    "La Elipa new all-electric centre (318 points, 20 MW)": (112.12, {2027: 1 / 3, 2028: 1 / 3, 2029: 1 / 3}),
}, "V", "Sanchinarro: EMT award Mar 2026, EUR 12,581,413.59 excl. VAT, 12 months; La Elipa: award to OHLA-Seranco, EUR 112,119,303 "
        "excl. VAT (tender budget EUR 134.3 m), up to 32 months from signing (https://diario.madrid.es/blog/notas-de-prensa/"
        "emt-madrid-adjudica-la-ejecucion-de-las-obras-del-nuevo-centro-de-operaciones-de-la-elipa/); year split is an assumption (A)",
        "capex_meur, both scenarios")
POINTS_COMMITTED = {2027: 114, 2029: 318}            # points those projects add, from the year they finish
S0_DELIVERIES = assume("S0 adjusted pace: net zero-emission buses added per year (D3)", {2026: 70, 2027: 65}, "V",
                       "2026: EMT 2026 budget, 70 e-buses for EUR 47.7 m; 2027: EMT 2027 draft budget, 65 e-buses for EUR 34.3 m "

                       "50 kept as a sensitivity. From 2028 no tender is announced, so the unadjusted 2021-25 pace "
                       f"({S0_PACE_UNADJUSTED:.1f}/yr, §3) continues", "File 4 S0", "2027 = 50; unadjusted pace every year")
ZE_ONLY_FROM = assume("Year from which every S0 replacement is zero-emission (D5)", 2030, "V",
                      "Regulation (EU) 2024/1610: 90 % of new city buses zero-emission from 2030, 100 % from 2035 "
                      "(https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/road-transport/lorries-buses-and-coaches_en); "
                      "EMT buying only zero-emission from 2030 is the team's reading (A)", "File 4 S0 from 2030", "90 % share 2030-34")
NO_GAS_PURCHASES = assume("No gas bus is bought in either scenario (D8)", True, "A",
                          "Team decision, 24 Nov 2026: no gas-bus order for 2026 or later is evidenced; EMT's 2026 and 2027 budgets buy "
                          "e-buses only", "File 4 S0 2026-2029", "S0 refills with gas until 2029")
def s0_pace(y):
    return S0_DELIVERIES.get(y, round(S0_PACE_UNADJUSTED))

# Service km (brief: 365 equivalent service days) and the standard/articulated mix, from File 2
KM_YEAR = file2.daily_km.sum() * P["service_days"]
ART_KM_SHARE = assume("Articulated share of service km (all technologies, all years)",

                      "File 2: km on articulated lines / total km; applied to BEV, H2 and CNG alike", "energy, CNG, CO2")
def mix(d):
    return (1 - ART_KM_SHARE) * d["Standard"] + ART_KM_SHARE * d["Articulated"]
KWH_KM, CNG_KG_KM = mix(P["kwh_km"]), mix(P["cng_kg_km"])
S25 = ZE25 / FLEET                                   # 2025 zero-emission share of fleet and of km (counterfactual)

      f"2025 ZE share {S25:.1%}")

Fleet model. Each year: buses past their 13-year life retire; the zero-emission target sets how many battery buses are bought (S0: 70, 65, then 77 a year; S1: File 2's line plan, with 2026 equal to the 70 delivered). If retirements do not leave enough room, the oldest gas buses retire early. Neither scenario buys gas (D8): a worn gas bus keeps running until its e-bus arrives (_deferred). From 2030 S0 replaces every retiring bus with an e-bus (D5). Energy, CNG, CO₂ and the 2025-frozen counterfactual follow from the km allocation. Columns starting with _ are diagnostics, not written to File 4.
